metadata.name: CHA2DS2-VASc score
metadata.summary: 9-point thromboembolic stroke risk score in non-valvular atrial fibrillation.
clinical_pearls: Female sex (Sc) alone without other risk factors (score 1 in women) does not by itself trigger anticoagulation in major AF guidelines.
Helps distinguish truly low-risk from elevated-risk AF patients, though overall discrimination is modest and must be paired with clinical judgment.

Pitfall — Special cardiomyopathies: 2024 ESC AF guidelines do NOT recommend using CHA2DS2-VASc to guide stroke prevention in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or cardiac amyloidosis (anticoagulate regardless of score).
Pitfall — Uncaptured thrombotic risks: Additional factors not included in the score (such as impaired renal function or active malignancy) can worsen thromboembolic risk and affect score performance.

interpretation.label: Low Risk (Score 0)
interpretation.summary: Score 0: truly low thromboembolic risk (~0–0.2%/year); anticoagulation generally not indicated.

interpretation.label: Intermediate / Sex-Modified Risk (Score 1)
interpretation.summary: Score 1: consider oral anticoagulation in men; if score is 1 solely due to female sex, anticoagulation is generally not indicated.

interpretation.label: Elevated Thromboembolic Risk (Score >= 2)
interpretation.summary: Score >= 2: oral anticoagulation recommended (barring contraindications; note female sex-only modifier if total = 2 in women with 1 non-sex factor).

assessment_guides.title: Female Sex Risk-Modifier Rule
bedside_steps: Count non-sex risk factors first when applying guideline anticoagulation thresholds.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Score 1 in a female with zero other risk factors carries the same low risk as score 0 in a male.
Any prior ischemic stroke or TIA automatically adds +2 points, placing the patient in the anticoagulation-indicated stratum.
